title: Workflow and State-Machine Design
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of workflow and state-machine design and at least two listed subtopics.

content.intro: Learn workflow and state-machine design through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Workflow and State-Machine Design matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines workflow and state-machine design as part of advanced django architecture. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Modeling states and allowed transitions; Validating transitions; Transaction-safe updates; Audit history; Preventing conflicting concurrent actions. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Modeling states and allowed transitions
items.text: Modeling states and allowed transitions affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Validating transitions
items.text: For Validating transitions, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Transaction-safe updates
items.text: Transaction-safe updates is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
